advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the browser-fixture skip-scan actually visited the expected e2e files (non-empty, includes known files) before trusting an empty offenders list.
evidence: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / E2E_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "tests" / "e2e" — a path miscomputation makes rglob empty and the anti-regression scan pass vacuously
ABSENCE: no assertion that any expected file (e.g. conftest.py or test_editor_browser.py) appeared among the scanned paths
advisory.finding: The AST scan test_no_browser_fixture_falls_back_to_a_bare_skip iterates E2E_DIR.rglob('*.py') and asserts offenders==[], but never asserts that any files (or any e2e test files) were actually visited. If E2E_DIR is miscomputed or the tree is relocated, rglob yields nothing, offenders stays empty, and the test passes green having scanned zero files — the guard cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never ran'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect the scanned paths and assert a known-present file (e.g. E2E_DIR/'conftest.py') and E2E_DIR/'test_editor_browser.py' were among them, so an empty glob fails loudly instead of passing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the skipif scan visited at least the known e2e modules before trusting its empty result.
evidence: ABSENCE: no liveness assertion that the walk produced any files
advisory.finding: The AST scan test_no_e2e_module_hides_a_test_behind_a_bare_skipif iterates E2E_DIR.rglob('*.py') and asserts offenders==[] without ever confirming any file was scanned; an empty glob (miscomputed E2E_DIR / relocated tree) passes the check having inspected nothing.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track scanned files and assert the count is non-zero and includes an expected module before asserting offenders==[].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the skip scan to also catch bare `skip(...)`/aliased imports of pytest.skip, or forbid such imports under tests/e2e.
advisory.finding: The pytest.skip AST detector only matches the attribute-call form pytest.skip(...) (node.func.value.id == 'pytest'); a reintroduced silent skip written as `from pytest import skip; skip(...)` or via an alias would not be flagged, leaving a gap in the anti-regression guarantee.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST/substring source scan in test_guard_reads_no_environment_and_knows_no_ci_provider with a behavioral assertion (invoke tier_unavailable with CI-style env vars present vs absent and assert identical outcome).
evidence: tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py:184 `assert "os" not in imported, "the guard must not consult the process environment"`
tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py:186-187 loops over provider substrings and asserts `provider not in lowered`

GUARD_PATH is tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py, the executable source under test (imported as `guard` at line 51), so the assertion targets implementation text, not observable behavior; the same portability property could be driven behaviorally (invoke tier_unavailable with CI-style env vars set vs unset and assert identical skip/fail outcome).
advisory.finding: test_guard_reads_no_environment_and_knows_no_ci_provider verifies the portability contract ('behaves identically with or without a CI provider') by AST-scanning imports and substring-scanning the implementation text of the unit under test (_browser_tier.py) rather than by driving the code — this is source-grepping / a change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. `import os` added purely for `os.PathLike` typing, or renaming a provider-naming comment) and passes even if the guard read the environment via a name not in the banned substring list.
scenarios: A maintainer adds `import os` for a typing/path helper that never reads the environment — the test fails though behavior is unchanged.
The guard is refactored to read the environment through a helper whose name is not in the provider list — the test still passes, missing the real regression.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that the announcement warning includes the recorded reason text (not just NOT_RUN_BANNER).
evidence: tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py:84 `with pytest.warns(guard.WARNING_CATEGORY, match=guard.NOT_RUN_BANNER):` — matches only the banner, never the reason body
advisory.finding: No test asserts that the recorded `reason` is carried into the announcement warning text, though _announce is added by this diff and its docstring claims it 'Carries the recorded reasoning in full'; test_a_licensed_non_execution_warns_so_the_summary_shows_it only matches on NOT_RUN_BANNER, so a regression that dropped the reason from the warning would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor of _announce drops the reason line while keeping the banner — the warning-summary contract silently regresses with all tests green.
